name: Tute gana-pierde
description: Tute gana-pierde: win-lose Tute variant. First to reach target wins; or lose condition. 40-card Spanish.

overview.description: Tute gana-pierde: win-lose Tute variant. First to reach target wins; or lose condition. 40-card Spanish.

history.origins: Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the most popular card games there. Tute gana-pierde is a Spanish variant in which the player with the most points loses unless someone reaches 101 or more to win; it is played by three to five players individually.
timeline: 19th century: Tute spread to Spain; gana-pierde (win-lose) variant emerged with target 101 and most-points-loses rule.

setup.deck: Standard Spanish 40-card pack (four suits: Oros, Copas, Espadas, Bastos; ranks 2–7 plus Sota, Caballo, Rey, As).
setup.dealing: All cards dealt one at a time anticlockwise; last card exposed for trump.

rules.objective: Avoid taking the most points; or reach 101 or more points to win and make all others lose. The player with the most points (under 101) loses unless someone reaches 101+.
rules.gameplay: All 40 cards dealt singly; last card exposed for trump. Player to dealer's right leads; follow suit and beat or trump per Tute rules. After winning a trick, a player may sing 40 (king-horse of trumps) or 20 (king-horse of another suit). Last trick winner may take or decline 10 extra points. Count points individually; most points loses, or 101+ wins.
keyRules: Gana-pierde: most points loses unless someone reaches 101+ to win.
Follow suit and beat or trump when able.
Sing 40 or 20 after winning a trick (king-horse in trumps or other suit).
Last trick: winner may claim or decline 10 points.

scoring.description: Points from cards in tricks, last trick 10, singing 40 or 20. Reach 101+ to win; else most points loses.
scoring.winCondition: Reach 101 or more points to win; otherwise the player with the most points loses.
